title: Choose the visual world for Samudra Kar's portfolio
question: The roll assigned the Cyanotype Orrery. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Cyanotype Orrery
options.lineage: brass orreries, celestial atlas plates and sun-printed cyanotypes
options.thesis: Seven worlds in one working instrument: the portfolio is an orrery you turn by scrolling, with Samudra at the centre.
materials: enamel planets in each world's own colour
options.viewport: Name set huge in expanded caps on the left; on the right a line-drawn orrery with seven dashed orbits, one solid for the world in conjunction, labels set along the rings, a readout naming it; Enter the worlds as the primary action.
options.risk: Space imagery slides toward the near-black-and-neon cliché if the blue ground and engraved line discipline slip.

raised.raise: Honest physics: orbit speed follows scroll velocity and every control has an instrument verb (turn, align, enter), never decoration.
Hierarchy by type size alone: no cards, boxes or badges; the active world is bigger, the rest step down.
Committed vs available states: unselected orbits and frames are dashed, the committed one is solid, everywhere on the site.
Labels ride the rings: names, numbers and readouts are set along orbit paths and the dial rim, the centre held quiet.

options.label: Contact Sheet
options.lineage: 35mm contact sheets, grease pencil and the photographer's loupe
options.thesis: One roll of film: seven projects are frames, the circled ones are selects, and a loupe under the cursor shows each world up close.
options.viewport: Two film strips frame a condensed name; frame 4A is circled in grease pencil, a loupe magnifies the frame under the pointer.
options.risk: Familiar: dark photography portfolios are where many personal sites land, and it leans on a facet (photography) with no photos on hand.

options.label: Session Title Card
options.thesis: Every project is a numbered session cut like a title frame: flat colour fields, colliding caps, hard cuts on the beat.
options.viewport: Mustard field sliced by a teal bar and a brick column, the name crashing in tight caps, the buddy as a freeze-frame silhouette, a numbered session strip along the bottom.
options.case: Wins on product clarity (numbered running order, project names at poster scale); ties on audience identification, and sits closest to the current loud style.
options.risk: Can read as a costume of a specific show if the bars and grain are applied without the beat-cut structure.

options.label: Safelight Darkroom
options.thesis: Projects develop like prints: test strips preview a world, the timer runs, and the image emerges as you scroll.
options.viewport: Safelight-red room, stepped test strips on the right with one print developing, the name in amber, a timer readout.
options.case: Holds audience identification through the photography facet; loses product clarity because worlds hide until developed.
options.risk: Monochrome red wash fights the seven worlds' own palettes and is hard on contrast.

options.label: Suminagashi Basin
options.thesis: The page is a basin of ink the cursor stirs.
options.viewport: A basin of marbled currents with a quiet name in the margin.
options.case: Loses both axes: the seven worlds dissolve into swirls and recruiters lose the project list.
options.kept: Honest physics: every motion obeys a real rule with a real name.
options.risk: Beautiful and unreadable as a portfolio.

options.label: Fight Poster
options.thesis: Two names collide at a versus mark.
options.viewport: A versus split with the undercard shrinking below.
options.case: Loses both axes: nothing in the portfolio is a comparison.

options.label: Sewing Pattern
options.thesis: Projects as numbered pattern pieces on tissue.
options.viewport: An envelope front indexing views A to G.
options.case: Loses both axes: the metaphor has nothing to do with the work.
options.kept: Dashed for available, solid for committed.

options.label: Accretion Disk
options.viewport: A glowing disk with labels orbiting the rim.
options.case: Loses both axes against the orrery: same orbit idea, darker, glowier and closer to the neon cliché.
options.kept: Labels set along the rings, the centre held quiet.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean developer portfolio: big name, short intro, a grid of project cards, about, contact.
canonCard.viewport: Name and one-line intro, buttons for work and contact, a 3-up grid of project cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from thousands of student portfolios by design; the seven worlds become thumbnails.
